column4: Summary
column5: Description

column4: Discovery & problem validation
column5: Prove the problem before building: golfers who know when they can play, but not where, check course booking pages one at a time because Utah tee sheets are split across city, county and private systems.

column4: Tee-time data layer
column5: The feasibility risk. A clean, fresh record for every open time (spots, price with fees, walking, rate rules) so nothing the golfer sees is ever generated.

column4: AI search & ranking
column5: The wedge. Turn 'Saturday morning, under $45, near Sandy, walking' into filters, rank every open time by fit, and explain the tradeoff in one line.

column4: Golfer search & booking experience
column5: One window plus constraints in, ranked shortlist out, then a handoff to the course's own booking page. Built for the Window Golfer and Group Organizer.

column4: Evals, trust & human-in-the-loop
column5: Place every task on the jagged frontier, set the eval bar before results are seen, and keep times and prices traceable to a real record.

column4: Launch & measurement
column5: Define success as an outcome, cut v1 scope, pilot in Salt Lake, then expand statewide.

column4: Problem statement with sourced fragmentation evidence
column5:
Golfers who know when but not where check each course one at a time.
AC:
- Every claim tagged sourced, secondhand or synthesis
- SLC city, county and private booking systems documented with links
- Evidence gap stated: nothing first-party yet

column4: JTBD job map and 10 scored desired outcomes (Ulwick ODI)
column5:
Core job: get a round on the calendar within the window I have free.
AC:
- 8-step job map with the struggle located (Locate, Prepare)
- 10 outcome statements scored Importance + max(Imp - Sat, 0)
- All ratings labeled hypotheses until interviews replace them

column4: Circumstance-based segments and beachhead pick
column5:
Beachhead: Window Golfer, with Group Organizer close behind.
AC:
- 5 segments cut by circumstance, not demographics
- Each segment mapped to its top outcomes and today's workaround
- Beachhead rationale written and flagged as synthesis

column4: Opportunity solution tree: 1 outcome, 3 opportunities, 6 solutions
column5:
Target 'know which option fits'; treat 'see every open time' as table stakes.
AC:
- Outcome is product-movable, not revenue
- 2 competing solutions per opportunity
- Cheapest test named for the riskiest solution in each branch

column4: Competitive scan of 8 tee-time tools
column5:
Quick Tee Times, Open Course, Supreme Golf, GolfNow/TeeOff, Chronogolf, SLC Golf, Stymie, Golf Utah.
AC:
- What each does for this job and the gap we can use
- Conclusion stated: time-window search exists, so we win on fit, not coverage

column4: Assumption map: 7 assumptions with pass thresholds set before testing
column5:
Riskiest (updated Nov 21): golfers want a dedicated app instead of asking ChatGPT or Claude, which can now book tee times through Noteefy and PRIMO.
AC:
- Each assumption typed (desirability, usability, feasibility, viability)
- Each has a test and a pass threshold written before results
- Assistant-vs-app test added: pass if 5 of 8 golfers prefer ours
- Fallback named if it fails: lead with group coordination

column4: Interview 8 Utah golfers on their last booking
column5:
Past behavior, not opinions: 'walk me through the last time you booked.'
AC:
- 8 interviews: at least 4 Window Golfers, 2 Group Organizers
- Answers logged against assumptions 1, 2, 3 and 5
- Hypothesized importance/satisfaction ratings updated or killed

column4: Test ranked shortlist vs. plain list side by side
column5:
Tests assumption 3 before building the ranking engine.
AC:
- Two clickable mocks on the same mock tee-sheet data
- Shown to 8 golfers in random order
- Pass: 6 of 8 pick the ranked version; decision logged

column4: One-page PRD for Tee Time Finder v1
column5:
Problem, JTBD, beachhead, v1 scope, out of scope, success metrics, open questions.
AC:
- Every requirement traces to an opportunity on the tree
- Updated with interview findings, not written before them

column4: Define the tee-time record schema
column5:
Fields: course, date/time, open spots, holes (9/18), green fee, fees, cart/walking, resident or pass rate flag, booking URL, source system, fetched_at.
AC:
- Every field has a type and an allowed range
- Every field the ranking uses exists in the schema
- Missing values have an explicit 'unknown' state, never a guess

column4: Build a mock tee-sheet dataset for 8-12 Utah courses
column5:
Class-scope stand-in for real feeds (assumption 6).
AC:
- Mix of SLC city, Salt Lake County and private courses
- Two weekends of realistic slots, prices and spot counts
- Labeled as mock everywhere it appears

column4: Course rules table: booking windows, resident rates, walking
column5:
Rule interpretation is jagged for AI, so store it as structured data.
AC:
- One row per course, each value with a source link
- Every row verified by a human before use
- Last-verified date shown

column4: Spike: real data access via tee-sheet partners vs. scraping
column5:
Timeboxed 3 days. Data access is the existential risk for the real product.
AC:
- Partner/API options listed for Chronogolf, GolfNow and course-run systems
- Terms-of-service risk noted for each
- Go / no-go recommendation written up

column4: Freshness: 'checked X min ago' and recheck before handoff
column5:
Targets outcome 8: slot gone between finding and booking.
AC:
- Every result shows its fetched_at age
- Slot rechecked when the golfer taps book
- Gone slots removed with a plain message

column4: Natural-language request to structured filters parser
column5:
'Saturday 7-11, under $45, 25 min from Sandy, walking, 3 of us' becomes filters.
AC:
- Outputs only fields in the record schema
- Ambiguous inputs trigger one clarifying question, not a guess
- Parsed filters shown as editable chips

column4: Rank open times by constraint fit
column5:
Deterministic score first; the LLM explains, it does not rank.
AC:
- Weights for price, drive time, time-in-window and walking documented
- Ranking uses only record fields
- Same inputs always return the same order

column4: One-line 'why this time' explanation
column5:
e.g., '$8 more than #2, but 12 minutes closer and walkable.'
AC:
- References only values in the record and the golfer's filters
- Never writes a time, price or spot count itself
- Passes the traceability guardrail

column4: Draft a group message with the top 2-3 options
column5:
Targets outcome 5: getting the group to agree on one option.
AC:
- Golfer edits and sends it; the app never sends for them
- Each option links to its live slot

column4: Wireframe the search: one window plus constraints
column5:
AC:
- Typed request or quick filters, golfer's choice
- Search entered in under 30 seconds in 5 hallway tests
- Mobile-first layout

column4: Results screen: ranked shortlist with total price and drive time
column5:
AC:
- Top 5 ranked times, each with total price (fees included), drive time and spots left
- Parsed-filter chips visible above results
- 'See all times' fallback to the full unranked list

column4: Hand off booking to the course's own system
column5:
Book and pay stays with the golfer and the course.
AC:
- Deep link opens the course booking page at the chosen time when the system allows
- Players and time carried over where possible
- Handoff tap logged for the North Star

column4: Alerts when a time opens in a saved window
column5:
Targets outcome 3. Parity with Quick Tee Times' scans, not a differentiator.
AC:
- Golfer saves a window and constraints
- Alert fires only for times that fit all constraints
- At most one alert per window per hour

column4: Golden parse set: 50 real phrasings labeled with correct filters
column5:
Ground truth for every parser change. Phrasings collected from interviews and golfers' own texts.
AC:
- 50 requests covering time, price, distance, walking, holes, group size and slang
- Each labeled with the correct filter set
- Versioned; never used for prompt tuning

column4: Set the ship bar before results are seen
column5:
Proposed bar (to validate): 90%+ of golden set fully correct; zero results untraceable to a record.
AC:
- Bar written and dated before the first eval run
- Failure categories defined so misses are fixable

column4: Map the jagged frontier for every step in the flow
column5:
Per the HBS Jagged Frontier case: parse (inside), rank and explain (inside, with care), report times and prices (outside, never generated), rate rules (jagged), book and pay (human).
AC:
- Every step classified with a reason
- Every human step has an owner

column4: Guardrail: every time and price traces to a source record
column5:
The one failure that kills trust: showing a time or price that doesn't exist.
AC:
- Automated check on 200 generated results and explanations
- Zero untraceable values before launch
- Check runs on every release

column4: Ranking agreement eval: top pick vs. the golfer's own pick
column5:
AC:
- 20 golfers pick from the same unranked list we rank
- Agreement rate recorded for top-1 and top-3
- Disagreements reviewed to adjust weights

column4: Define the North Star metric
column5:
Proposed: weekly rounds booked through handoff that fit the golfer's window and constraints. Outcome over output (Perri).
AC:
- Formula and data source documented
- Input metrics: searches completed, shortlist-to-handoff rate, filter-correction rate

column4: RICE-score the backlog to cut v1 scope
column5:
AC:
- Reach, Impact, Confidence, Effort filled for every To Do story
- v1 cut line drawn and defended

column4: Write pilot-quarter OKRs
column5:
Goal-setting, separate from prioritization.
AC:
- 1 objective, 3 measurable key results tied to the North Star

column4: Salt Lake pilot: 25 golfers over 4 weekends
column5:
Salt Lake first because discovery evidence is local; statewide Utah next.
AC:
- At least 100 completed searches
- Weekly readout: handoff rate, filter corrections, parse misses

column4: Post-round check: did the pick fit?
column5:
Closes the loop for the evals.
AC:
- One-tap question sent after the round
- Misses added as new labeled eval cases
